chunks: Ibn Mahbub, from 'Abbad ibn Suhayb, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

I heard him saying: Amir al-Mu'minin 'Ali عليه السلام used to say: “If a man says to another man, ‘O ma'fuj,’ and ‘O one who has been sexually penetrated in his anus,’ then the hadd punishment upon him is the hadd of the slanderer.”

key_terms.حَدَّ الْقَاذِفِ: the legal punishment of one who makes a slanderous sexual accusation
key_terms.عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: peace be upon him; honorific used for the Imam
key_terms.مَنْكُوحًا فِي دُبُرِهِ: one alleged to have been penetrated in his anus
key_terms.يَا مَعْفُوجُ: an abusive epithet implying sexual disgrace

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone insults another man with words implying sexual violation or disgrace in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning abusive language that amounts to an accusation of sexual disgrace. Imam 'Ali عليه السلام is reported to have ruled that such speech incurs the hadd penalty of qadhf, treating it as defamatory accusation with legal consequence.
